notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Milestone 1 is intentionally boring: replace .env first. Vercel/GitHub sync, drift detection, expiry automation, rotation, MCP, teams and fine-grained agent policy are explicitly deferred.

notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Authentication architecture for M1: Better Auth backed by PostgreSQL; self-hosted must support local account/passkey without Kinde or another hosted auth dependency. CLI uses browser/device authorization and a revocable device identity. Vault unlock remains separate from login.

notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: This capability is now M2 and depends on M1 secure core.

problem: Local development commonly depends on persistent plaintext .env files that are manually distributed, copied and left readable by the local user context, tools, plugins and supply-chain code.
scope: Build on M1 secure core to replace the local plaintext .env workflow.
Implement the smallest end-to-end product slice that replaces a local plaintext .env workflow for one developer and one project.
Provide a control-plane Web UI to create a project, create a development environment and add or update secret name/value pairs.
Provide a local Rust binary with CLI entrypoints for login/unlock and sec run -- <command>.
Fetch the selected project/environment secrets, inject them only into the spawned child-process environment and do not materialize a plaintext .env file.
Record basic audit events for authentication, runtime start, secret-set names used, runtime stop and failures; audit data must never contain secret values.
Use a bounded local authenticated/unlocked session so repeated dev-server starts do not require repeated interactive authentication during the valid session.
Keep the implementation architecture compatible with later Vercel/GitHub synchronization, expiry lifecycle and MCP, but do not implement those capabilities in this milestone.
title: Milestone 2: replace local .env with runtime secrets
validation: A user can create a project and development environment in the Web UI and store all variables required by a sample Next.js application.
After authentication, sec run -- npm run dev starts the sample Next.js server with the required variables visible through process.env.
The complete happy path works without creating or requiring .env, .env.local or another plaintext secret file in the project directory.
Restarting the child process during a valid local session does not require re-entering credentials or reconfiguring secrets.
Stopping or crashing the child process leaves no plaintext secret file behind.
The audit view shows who started the runtime, project, environment, secret names/count, timestamps and outcome, but never secret values.
A fresh clone of the sample repository can be made runnable by installing/configuring the client and authenticating, without receiving an .env file out of band.
A self-hosted M1 instance can authenticate a user using a local account/passkey without Kinde or another mandatory hosted identity dependency.
The CLI can authorize a device through the browser, the control plane can list/revoke that device, and revocation prevents new runtime grants.
Project/environment authorization remains functional if the configured human identity provider is changed.
value: Deliver the first immediately useful product behavior: a developer can stop keeping a plaintext .env file while preserving an equally simple dev-server workflow.
Prove the local runtime-delivery path before adding synchronization, lifecycle automation or AI-specific features.
